Method of Attack: Ransomware infection distributed by Neutrino exploit kit using randomly named DLL files; encryption of files using AES-256 (CrypMIC) and RSA/RC4 combination (CryptXXX); attack vectors include malvertising and compromised websites; retrieval of encryption keys and ransom notes from C&C servers; information theft and system information sent to C&C
Impacted Systems: Windows systems with drives D to Z, %USERPROFILE%, removable and mapped network drives (CrypMIC); Windows systems with drives B to Z, removable and network drives (CryptXXX)
Indicators of Compromise: Randomly named DLL files (rad{randomhexcharacters}.tmp.dll); ransom note files: README.TXT, README.HTML, README.BMP (CrypMIC); !README.HTML, !README.BMP (CryptXXX); payment server login screens with distinct UI differences; personal ID formats in ransom notes: 4 groups of 8 hex characters separated by colons (CrypMIC), 12 hex characters (CryptXXX); network activity over TCP port 443; presence of information-stealing module fx100.dll (CryptXXX); shadow copies deletion using vssadmin (CrypMIC)
